name: Jellyfin Federation
overview: Allows jellyfin servers to federate with each other
description: This Jellyfin plugin allows multiple Jellyfin servers to federate, sharing media libraries in real-time without syncing or copying files. Media can be streamed from one server to another with live transcoding if necessary.

versions.changelog: Federated episodes no longer show 'Missing' in the UI. They were materialized as their base Jellyfin CLR types with Path null, so LocationType resolved to Virtual - and the web client paints a 'Missing' badge on any episode with Type == Episode && LocationType == Virtual. Federated items are now created under dedicated subclasses (FederatedEpisode, FederatedMovie, ...) that report LocationType = Remote. One-time rebuild of existing federated items (watch/playback progress on them is reset once).

Fix playback for federated items lacking a configured remote UserId: PlaybackInfo now falls back to the remote's first user automatically (previously it returned null, so media sources carried no Container/MediaStreams and every client reported 'Unable to find a valid media source to play'). Adds logs to confirm stream info is resolved.

Federated seasons and episodes are visible without enabling 'Display missing episodes' (they were stamped IsVirtualItem, which Jellyfin reads as 'missing'). Seasons now carry their IndexNumber, so Jellyfin stops creating a duplicate empty season beside each real one; the duplicates it already created are removed on first sync. Media sources now carry the remote's real container and stream info, without which no client could validate playback. Rebuilds federated Series/Season/Episode items once on upgrade.
Debug logging for the 'unable to find a valid media source' playback error (seasons/episodes are now visible, so this is the next thing to fix). No database changes in this release.

The 0.0.16 fix only recreated Season/Episode items, not the Series itself - a Series never got its own PresentationUniqueKey set, so the match could still fail depending on a library setting. Series are now included in the migration too.

Fix: saving config (from any page load) silently reset the migration-complete flag, since the config page's save payload doesn't include newer fields - causing the whole episode migration to destructively rerun on every config save.

Actual fix for invisible episodes: Jellyfin's show/season pages find children by a SeriesPresentationUniqueKey match, not by parent/ancestor id. Federated episodes never had it set. One-time migration backfills it.
Fix: startup sync and the scheduled sync could run at the same time and corrupt each other mid-migration (SQLite lock errors). Syncs are now serialized, and the migration runs once more cleanly.
One-time migration: recreates existing seasons/episodes so 0.0.13's ordering fix actually applies to them (not just newly-synced ones).
Create shows/seasons/episodes in order (parent before child) so ancestry resolves correctly for browsing.
Fix: seasons were deleted right after being created, so episodes never persisted (no seasons, nothing playable).
Debug logging for the no-seasons/can't-play issue.
TV episodes now sync and play. Fixed duplicate/mismatched-watched-state shows and content looping back in from federated servers.
Actual fix for the missing-movies issue (wrong parent folder).
More debug logging for the missing-movies issue.
Debug logging for the missing-movies issue.

Fix: federated items were saved to the database as orphans, so they never appeared in any library. ILibraryManager.CreateItems does not parent the items it saves - its parent argument only feeds the ItemAdded event - and the plugin never set ParentId itself. The rows therefore matched neither the direct-children query (ParentId) nor the recursive one (AncestorIds, which Jellyfin derives from the ParentId chain at save time), leaving them invisible in the UI and invisible to the plugin's own existence check, which is why every sync re-reported the entire library as newly created. Items are now parented to their provisioned library folder. Item ids are derived deterministically from the cache key, so existing orphaned rows are adopted in place on the next sync - no manual cleanup or database reset needed. Also aligns the repository manifest guid with the plugin's actual id.

Fix: federated items never showed up. Materialized items had Path set to a federation:// URI Jellyfin doesn't recognize, so it treated them as missing/offline everywhere - hidden from browsing and from the plugin's own dedup check, which silently recreated a full duplicate set every hour. Items are now identified by a FederationKey provider id instead, with Path left null (true Virtual item). Upgrading auto-cleans any legacy federation:// duplicates on the next sync, no manual steps needed. Also triggers a background sync 5s after server start so items appear without waiting for the first scheduled task.

Fix: virtual libraries now actually provision. Jellyfin's AddVirtualFolder requires real filesystem paths, so federation:// URIs were rejected. Now uses an empty shadow folder under the plugin data dir; same-name libraries merge into one. Removal only detaches the federation location from merged libraries.
Config page rewrite: sidebar link, guided setup, working buttons, auto-detect public URL. Same-name libraries across servers merge into one. Advanced settings collapsed by default.
